title_zh: 反式白藜芦醇通过人体重建表皮中的芳烃受体途径减轻炎症并改善皮肤屏障功能。
source_body_en: OBJECTIVE: The aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AHR) is a regulator of epidermal homeostasis and a promising target for cosmetic and dermatological ingredients aimed at improving skin barrier function and reducing inflammation. This study investigated the potential of the natural polyphenol trans-resveratrol (RSV), a compound of cosmetic interest, to modulate downstream AHR signalling and restore epidermal integrity in a model of skin compromised by a pro-inflammatory environment. METHODS: A reconstructed human epidermis (RhE) was exposed to a cytokine cocktail (IL-4, IL-13, TNF-α) to induce a phenotype mimicking some aspects of atopic eczema, namely inflammation, oxidative stress and barrier disruption, features also prevalent in sensitive and reactive skin conditions. The effects of RSV were evaluated by assessing inflammatory mediators, oxidative stress-related markers, aryl hydrocarbon receptor signalling and epidermal barrier-associated proteins using molecular, biochemical and histological analyses. RESULTS: Cytokine exposure induced a pronounced inflammatory response, activation of aryl hydrocarbon receptor signalling, oxidative stress-related gene expression and dysregulation of barrier-related markers. Treatment with RSV attenuated the inflamed phenotype by reducing IL1A mRNA expression and IL-1α secretion, attenuating oxidative stress-associated AHR target gene responses through downregulation of CYP1A1 and CYP1B1, while maintaining AHR and HMOX1 expression and modulating barrier-associated gene expression, particularly by downregulating CASP14 and upregulating the tight junction protein occludin (OCLN). CONCLUSION: These findings provide mechanistic evidence in a human epidermis model that RSV can counteract inflammation, mitigate oxidative stress and support epidermal barrier homeostasis, actions mediated, at least in part, through modulation of AHR downstream signalling. This supports the potential of resveratrol as a multifunctional active ingredient in cosmetic and dermatological formulations designed to strengthen the skin barrier and calm sensitive or compromised skin.
abstract_zh: 目的:芳烃受体(AHR)是表皮稳态的调节剂,也是化妆品和皮肤病成分的一个有前途的目标,旨在改善皮肤屏障功能和减少炎症。本研究调查了天然多酚反式白藜芦醇 (RSV)(一种化妆品化合物)在受促炎环境损害的皮肤模型中调节下游 AHR 信号并恢复表皮完整性的潜力。方法:将重建的人表皮 (RhE) 暴露于细胞因子混合物(IL-4、IL-13、TNF-α),以诱导模仿特应性湿疹某些方面的表型,即炎症、氧化应激和屏障破坏,这些特征在敏感和反应性皮肤状况中也很常见。通过使用分子、生化和组织学分析评估炎症介质、氧化应激相关标记物、芳烃受体信号传导和表皮屏障相关蛋白,评估 RSV 的影响。结果:细胞因子暴露诱导了明显的炎症反应、芳烃受体信号传导的激活、氧化应激相关基因的表达以及屏障相关标记物的失调。治疗 与 RSV 通过减少 IL1A mRNA 表达和 IL-1α 分泌来减轻炎症表型,通过下调 CYP1A1 和 CYP1B1 来减弱氧化应激相关的 AHR 靶基因反应,同时维持 AHR 和 HMOX1 表达并调节屏障相关基因表达,特别是通过下调 CASP14 和上调紧密连接蛋白 Occludin (OCLN)。结论:这些发现为人类表皮模型提供了机制证据,表明 RSV 可以对抗炎症、减轻氧化应激并支持表皮屏障稳态,这些作用至少部分是通过调节 AHR 下游信号传导介导的。这支持了白藜芦醇作为化妆品和皮肤病配方中的多功能活性成分的潜力,旨在增强皮肤屏障并镇静敏感或受损的皮肤。

title: Clinical characteristics and risk factors for poor prognosis of RSV lower respiratory tract infection: a two-center study
abstract: Abstract Objective Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of acute lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI) in children under five years of age. In this study, we investigated the value of simple and readily available clinical indicators in predicting poor prognosis in children with RSV-LRTI. Methods This was a retrospective cohort study of children with RSV-LRTI admitted to Children’s Hospital of Nanjing Medical University (April 2023–May 2024) and Gaoyou People’s Hospital (December 2024–June 2025). Demographic and clinical data were collected from patient records, and patients were stratified based on three adverse prognostic events: admission to Intensive Care Unit (ICU), prolonged hospital stay, and severe pneumonia. Results A total of 257 eligible children were enrolled, of whom 254 (98.8%) exhibited cough, 144 (56.0%) presented with wheezing and 194 (75.4%) developed febrile symptoms. 220 (85.6%) cases of RSV-LRTI occurred in winter and spring, with a higher proportion of cases occurring in infants under 1 year of age. A higher respiratory rate at admission was independently associated with ICU admission (Firth regression: OR 1.132, both P < 0.05), though this finding was limited by the small number of ICU cases. The presence of three concave sign was independently associated with prolonged hospital stay (OR 5.242, 95% CI 1.360-19.951, P = 0.017). Procalcitonin (PCT) was an independent risk factor for severe pneumonia (OR 1.616, 95% CI 1.074–2.837, P = 0.020). Conclusion Higher respiratory rate at admission was independently associated with ICU admission, and the presence of three concave sign was independently associated with prolonged hospital stay. PCT was an independent risk factor for severe pneumonia. These simple clinical indicators facilitate early identification of children at risk of adverse outcomes.

analysis.research_question_and_background: RSV is a leading cause of acute lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI) in children under five years of age, creating a need for simple clinical indicators to predict poor prognosis in RSV-LRTI.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This retrospective cohort study enrolled children with RSV-LRTI admitted to two hospitals in China between April 2023 and June 2025, collecting demographic and clinical data from patient records.
analysis.methods: Patients were stratified based on adverse prognostic events including ICU admission, prolonged hospital stay, and severe pneumonia, and associations were assessed using Firth regression models.
analysis.main_results: Among 257 children, 254 (98.8%) had cough, 144 (56.0%) wheezing, and 194 (75.4%) febrile symptoms; higher respiratory rate at admission was independently associated with ICU admission (OR 1.132, P < 0.05), the presence of three concave sign with prolonged hospital stay (OR 5.242, 95% CI 1.360–19.951, P = 0.017), and procalcitonin with severe pneumonia (OR 1.616, 95% CI 1.074–2.837, P = 0.020).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors conclude that simple clinical indicators such as respiratory rate, three concave sign, and procalcitonin can facilitate early identification of children at risk of adverse outcomes in RSV-LRTI.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings may inform early risk stratification and targeted interventions in pediatric RSV-LRTI to reduce severe outcomes and optimize resource use.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design, small number of ICU cases, and single-season data, warranting cautious interpretation and prospective validation.

analysis.summary_en: This two-center retrospective cohort study in China investigated simple clinical indicators to predict poor prognosis among 257 children hospitalized with RSV lower respiratory tract infection between April 2023 and June 2025. The study stratified patients by ICU admission, prolonged hospital stay, and severe pneumonia, and analyzed associations using Firth regression. Among enrolled children, nearly all presented with cough, over half with wheezing, and three-quarters with fever. Higher respiratory rate at admission was independently associated with ICU admission, the presence of three concave sign with prolonged hospital stay, and elevated procalcitonin with severe pneumonia. The authors propose that these readily available indicators can support early risk identification in pediatric RSV-LRTI. However, the retrospective design, small ICU subgroup, and single-season data limit causal inference and generalizability.

title_zh: RSV下呼吸道感染的临床特征及预后不良的危险因素:一项两中心研究
source_body_en: Abstract Objective Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of acute lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI) in children under five years of age. In this study, we investigated the value of simple and readily available clinical indicators in predicting poor prognosis in children with RSV-LRTI. Methods This was a retrospective cohort study of children with RSV-LRTI admitted to Children’s Hospital of Nanjing Medical University (April 2023–May 2024) and Gaoyou People’s Hospital (December 2024–June 2025). Demographic and clinical data were collected from patient records, and patients were stratified based on three adverse prognostic events: admission to Intensive Care Unit (ICU), prolonged hospital stay, and severe pneumonia. Results A total of 257 eligible children were enrolled, of whom 254 (98.8%) exhibited cough, 144 (56.0%) presented with wheezing and 194 (75.4%) developed febrile symptoms. 220 (85.6%) cases of RSV-LRTI occurred in winter and spring, with a higher proportion of cases occurring in infants under 1 year of age. A higher respiratory rate at admission was independently associated with ICU admission (Firth regression: OR 1.132, both P < 0.05), though this finding was limited by the small number of ICU cases. The presence of three concave sign was independently associated with prolonged hospital stay (OR 5.242, 95% CI 1.360-19.951, P = 0.017). Procalcitonin (PCT) was an independent risk factor for severe pneumonia (OR 1.616, 95% CI 1.074–2.837, P = 0.020). Conclusion Higher respiratory rate at admission was independently associated with ICU admission, and the presence of three concave sign was independently associated with prolonged hospital stay. PCT was an independent risk factor for severe pneumonia. These simple clinical indicators facilitate early identification of children at risk of adverse outcomes.

title: Recent Advances in CRISPR/Cas Systems for Respiratory Pathogen Diagnostics
abstract: Early, rapid, and accurate detection is essential for clinical management and epidemiological control of acute respiratory infections caused by pathogens. Traditional testing methods such as microbial culture, serological testing, and PCR are restrictive in terms of operation and logistics and are therefore not easily used in point-of-care settings. The CRISPR/Cas system is an adaptive prokaryotic immune system composed of clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats and their associated proteins, which has been used as a nucleic acid diagnostic platform with programmable sequence-specific target recognition and signal-amplifying collateral cleavage activity. Existing reviews have mostly focused on the classification of Cas enzymes or amplification strategies; in this review, a pathogen-centric approach was taken, covering viral pathogens (SARS-CoV-2, influenza virus, RSV, HAdV and VZV), bacterial pathogens (Mycobacterium tuberculosis, Streptococcus pneumoniae, Mycoplasma pneumoniae and Staphylococcus aureus) and fungal pathogens (Aspergillus fumigatus and Pneumocystis jirovecii). Key technological advances, such as isothermal amplification coupling, single-vessel integrated reaction designs, amplification-free digital detection, and electrochemical biosensor integration, are evaluated for Cas9-, Cas12-, and Cas13-based systems, with their mechanistic bases outlined. The current challenges that hinder clinical translation, such as sample matrix interference, multiple signal cross-talk, crRNA off-target effects, and the lack of large-scale validation studies, are critically assessed. At the same time, future pathways for portable, integrated, and inexpensive diagnostic platforms are suggested.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines the application of CRISPR/Cas systems for early, rapid, and accurate detection of acute respiratory infections, focusing on viral pathogens including respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) as a target entity. The central question addresses the suitability of CRISPR/Cas-based diagnostics for point-of-care settings in managing RSV and related respiratory infections.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This is a pathogen-centric review evaluating CRISPR/Cas systems for diagnostic applications. It assesses technological advances such as isothermal amplification coupling, single-vessel integrated reaction designs, amplification-free digital detection, and electrochemical biosensor integration across Cas9-, Cas12-, and Cas13-based systems. The review critically examines challenges including sample matrix interference, signal cross-talk, crRNA off-target effects, and the lack of large-scale validation studies.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The CRISPR/Cas system offers programmable sequence-specific target recognition and signal-amplifying collateral cleavage activity, making it a promising platform for nucleic acid diagnostics of respiratory pathogens. Key technological advances in Cas9-, Cas12-, and Cas13-based systems are highlighted as foundational for developing portable, integrated, and inexpensive diagnostic platforms.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identifies critical challenges hindering clinical translation, including sample matrix interference, multiple signal cross-talk, crRNA off-target effects, and the lack of large-scale validation studies. These gaps underscore the need for further methodological refinement and empirical validation before widespread adoption.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Future research should prioritize addressing sample matrix interference, optimizing signal specificity, and conducting large-scale validation studies to enable clinical translation of CRISPR/Cas-based diagnostics. Development of portable, integrated, and inexpensive platforms is suggested to enhance point-of-care applicability for respiratory pathogen detection.

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates CRISPR/Cas systems as nucleic acid diagnostic platforms for respiratory pathogens, with a focus on respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). title: A Combined Intranasal and Parenteral Vaccination Strategy Reduces Morbidity and Antimicrobial Treatments Associated with Bovine Respiratory Disease in Danish Commercial Veal Calves
abstract: Background: Bovine respiratory disease (BRD) is a major driver of antimicrobial use in veal calf production systems. Although vaccination may reduce disease incidence and antimicrobial treatments, field evidence supporting clinically relevant reductions in antimicrobial use remains limited. This study evaluated the clinical efficacy of a combined intranasal (IN) and parenteral (subcutaneous/intramuscular; SC/IM) vaccination strategy targeting bovine respiratory syncytial virus, Histophilus somni, and Mannheimia haemolytica under commercial conditions. Methods: A randomised controlled field trial was conducted on two Danish veal calf farms between November 2019 and April 2020, including 880 calves allocated to a vaccinated group (n = 445) or an unvaccinated control group (n = 435). Health outcomes included morbidity, antimicrobial use, mortality, growth performance, and slaughterhouse pulmonary and pleural lesions and were analysed using mixed-effects models. Results: Vaccination significantly reduced BRD-associated morbidity across all evaluation periods (from day 5 after arrival to slaughter), with relative reductions of 18.8–24.6% and 30% fewer antimicrobial treatment days. Pulmonary and pleural lesions were significantly less frequent in vaccinated calves (≈36% reduction). No statistically significant differences were observed in growth performance or mortality. Conclusions: Combined IN + SC/IM vaccination was associated with lower BRD-associated morbidity, antimicrobial treatments, and slaughterhouse respiratory lesions under commercial conditions.

title: Clinical characteristics and factors associated with severe disease in hospitalized infants with human metapneumovirus pneumonia and respiratory bacterial co-detection: a single-center retrospective study
abstract: Background Human metapneumovirus (hMPV) is an important cause of lower respiratory tract infection in infants, but data on infants with respiratory bacterial co-detection are limited. We aimed to describe the clinical and microbiological characteristics of this population and to explore factors associated with severe disease. Methods We conducted a single-center retrospective study of infants aged 12 months or younger who were hospitalized at Henan Children's Hospital between October 2024 and March 2025 with hMPV pneumonia and clinically adjudicated respiratory bacterial co-detection. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, imaging, treatment, and 6-month follow-up data were extracted from medical records. Severe disease was classified according to the pediatric community-acquired pneumonia guideline and the discharge diagnosis. Group comparisons used chi-square or Fisher's exact tests and the Mann–Whitney U test. Exploratory logistic regression was performed; the primary model excluded lethargy because it overlapped with severity criteria, and a secondary warning-sign model included lethargy. Results Among 309 infants, 190 (61.5%) were male and 42 (13.6%) were classified as severe cases. Streptococcus pneumoniae was the most frequently co-detected bacterium. Among 143 infants who underwent chest CT, multilobar pneumonia (90.9%) and ground-glass opacity (56.6%) were the most common findings. In the primary exploratory model, artificial feeding (OR 2.60, 95% CI 1.27–5.34), underlying diseases (OR 2.43, 95% CI 1.14–5.21), and lower albumin levels (OR 0.85 per 1 g/L increase, 95% CI 0.78–0.94) were associated with severe disease. In the secondary model, lethargy was strongly associated with severe presentation (OR 5.02, 95% CI 2.38–10.62) and should be interpreted as a warning sign rather than an independent causal factor. Conclusions Underlying diseases, artificial feeding, and lower albumin levels may help identify infants with hMPV pneumonia and respiratory bacterial co-detection who require closer monitoring. Lethargy should be regarded as an early warning sign. These association-based findings require confirmation in multicenter prospective studies with standardized pathogen quantification and adjudication.

Background Page 2/21 Lower respiratory tract infections are a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in infants and children worldwide [1–3]. Viral pneumonia accounts for a substantial proportion of these cases. Human metapneumovirus (hMPV), first identified in 2001, is an important respiratory pathogen with clinical manifestations that overlap with those of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) [4]. hMPV can infect individuals of all ages, but infants, young children, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals are particularly vulnerable. Globally, hMPV is considered one of the major viral causes of bronchiolitis and pneumonia in children under 5 years of age [5, 6]. In 2018, hMPV-associated acute lower respiratory infection caused a substantial burden among children under 5 years of age worldwide, including severe cases requiring hospitalization and deaths [7]. Previous studies on hMPV have mainly focused on epidemiological characteristics and general clinical features. However, data on hMPV pneumonia in infants, especially cases with bacterial co-detection or suspected bacterial coinfection, remain limited. Viral infection may impair the respiratory mucosal barrier and disrupt host immune responses, creating conditions that facilitate bacterial overgrowth or invasion and may aggravate pulmonary inflammation [8–10]. Nevertheless, detection of bacterial DNA in respiratory specimens does not by itself confirm invasive bacterial infection, especially for organisms that may colonize the upper airway, and therefore requires clinical adjudication. To address this gap, the present study focused on infants aged 12 months or younger with hMPV pneumonia and clinically adjudicated respiratory bacterial DNA co-detection after exclusion of cases considered to represent airway colonization. We systematically summarized their clinical characteristics, bacterial co-detection profile, imaging findings, treatment, short-term follow-up outcomes, and severity- associated clinical and laboratory features. The study aimed to provide descriptive evidence for early recognition and risk stratification of high-risk infants in clinical practice while avoiding interpretation of bacterial DNA positivity alone as evidence of concomitant bacterial pneumonia. Methods Study design, setting, and participants This single-center retrospective observational study included infants aged 12 months or younger who were hospitalized at Henan Children's Hospital (Zhengzhou Children's Hospital), Zhengzhou, China, from October 2024 to March 2025 with hMPV pneumonia and respiratory bacterial co-detection. Inclusion criteria were: (1) age ≤ 12 months at admission; (2) pneumonia diagnosed according to the Chinese pediatric community-acquired pneumonia guideline [11]; (3) hMPV confirmed by nucleic acid testing of a respiratory specimen; and (4) at least one bacterial pathogen detected in a respiratory specimen and judged clinically compatible with concomitant bacterial pneumonia rather than simple airway colonization. Exclusion criteria were: (1) nosocomial infection; (2) incomplete records; (3) clinically relevant co-detection of another respiratory virus; (4) clinically relevant co-detection of Mycoplasma pneumoniae, Chlamydia spp., fungi, or Mycobacterium tuberculosis; and (5) bacterial detection adjudicated as airway colonization. Severe disease was classified using the pediatric community- Page 3/21 acquired pneumonia guideline and the discharge diagnosis. The assessment considered respiratory distress, hypoxemia, systemic toxicity or altered mental status, severe complications, and the need for intensive supportive care. Infants who did not meet the severe-disease criteria were classified as non- severe. The study was approved by the Ethics Committee of Henan Children's Hospital (2025-IITGC-011- 001), which waived the requirement for informed consent because of the retrospective observational design. Specimen collection and microbiological testing Deep sputum, blood, and nasopharyngeal swab specimens were collected by trained staff using aseptic procedures within 24 h of admission and were tested in the institutional clinical laboratory. hMPV and bacterial targets were identified from routine nucleic-acid reports, and culture results were recorded when available. Pathogen-load information was extracted when reported. No additional microbiological testing was performed for this study. Clinical adjudication of bacterial infection versus airway colonization Bacterial colonization and possible concomitant bacterial pneumonia were differentiated by integrating clinical deterioration, inflammatory markers, chest imaging, reported pathogen load, culture results when available, and the treating team’s documented response assessment. Detection of low-load oropharyngeal commensal organisms without compatible clinical, inflammatory, or imaging evidence was classified as colonization and excluded. Because this retrospective adjudication did not use universal culture confirmation or a prospectively validated algorithm, the retained cohort is described as having clinically adjudicated bacterial co-detection rather than microbiologically proven bacterial pneumonia. Data collection and definitions Clinical data were extracted from the electronic inpatient record, including demographics, admission and discharge dates, symptoms, prematurity, feeding method, delivery mode, underlying diseases, laboratory tests within 24 h, chest imaging, treatments, ventilatory support, length of stay, and follow-up outcomes. Poor appetite was defined as a ≥ 50% reduction in daily food or milk intake from the pre-illness level for > 48 h. Underlying disease was coded when a chronic, congenital, genetic, metabolic, neurologic, cardiopulmonary, hematologic, or oncologic condition was documented. Wheezing was defined as a history of wheezing or wheezing during the current illness; this combined definition was used consistently in Fig. 2 and Table 3. Lethargy was based on admission documentation of poor mental status. Recurrent wheezing was defined as at least two parent-reported wheezing episodes after discharge or physician-diagnosed wheezing requiring medical care during the 6-month follow-up period. Statistical analysis Page 4/21 SPSS version 27.0 was used for statistical analysis. Continuous variables were assessed descriptively and are presented as median (Q1, Q3); categorical variables are presented as n (%). Between-group comparisons used the Mann–Whitney U test for continuous variables and the chi-square or Fisher’s exact test for categorical variables, as appropriate. No imputation was performed; available-case analysis was used. IL-6 was unavailable for 24 infants (3 severe and 21 non-severe), whereas variables included in the regression models were complete. Given 42 severe outcomes, the exploratory primary logistic regression model was restricted to three clinically selected variables: artificial feeding, underlying diseases, and albumin. A secondary warning-sign model added lethargy, which overlaps with severity classification and was therefore not treated as a causal predictor. Odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were reported; the OR for albumin represents a 1 g/L increase. No adjustment was made for multiple comparisons. All results were interpreted as associations, and two-sided P < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Results Underlying disease conditions Among the 309 included infants, 190 were male and 119 were female, and 42 were classified as severe cases. Fifty-four infants had at least one recorded underlying disease. The conditions included hematologic disorders, congenital heart disease, airway abnormalities, prematurity-related chronic lung disease, neurodevelopmental disorders, gastrointestinal disorders, tumors, and genetic or metabolic diseases (Supplementary Table S1). Seasonal and age distribution The number of enrolled infants increased from October, peaked in December, and then gradually decreased. Because the denominator of all tested or hospitalized infants by month was unavailable, this result represents the monthly distribution of enrolled cases rather than a monthly detection rate. Therefore, the seasonal pattern was interpreted descriptively (Fig. 1a). The age distribution of enrolled cases is shown in Fig. 1b. Clinical manifestations and laboratory results Of the 309 infants, 54 (17.5%) had complications and 38 (12.3%) were born prematurely. The most frequently recorded clinical features were cough (303/309, 98.1%), wheezing history or wheezing during the current illness (178/309, 57.6%), fever (159/309, 51.5%), poor appetite (147/309, 47.6%), rhinorrhea (144/309, 46.6%), nasal congestion (114/309, 36.9%), and vomiting (54/309, 17.5%) (Fig. 2). Laboratory testing showed WBC > 15×10^9/L in 28 infants (9.1%), NEUT% >50% in 67 (21.7%), CRP > 20 mg/L in 23 (7.4%), PCT > 0.5 ng/mL in 18 (5.8%), ALT > 70 U/L in 8 (2.6%), AST > 80 U/L in 12 (3.9%), LDH > 250 U/L in 271 (87.7%), TP < 55 g/L in 26 (8.4%), ALB < 39 g/L in 34 (11.0%), CK > 310 U/L in 9 (2.9%), and CK-MB ≥ 48 U/L in 15 (4.9%). Among the 285 infants with available IL-6 results, 89 (31.2%) had IL-6 > 20 pg/mL. Page 5/21 Imaging features Among the 143 infants who underwent complete chest CT examination, the most common findings were multilobar pneumonia (130/143, 90.9%), ground-glass opacity (81/143, 56.6%), airway narrowing of varying degrees (40/143, 28.0%), and pulmonary consolidation (24/143, 16.8%) (Fig. 3). These imaging findings refer to the CT-scanned subgroup rather than the entire cohort, and no inference was made regarding the prevalence of these CT abnormalities in all included infants. Airway narrowing mainly involved the right middle-lobe bronchus and the left main bronchus. Pulmonary consolidation included multilobar consolidation, right upper-lobe consolidation, left lower-lobe consolidation, pulmonary atelectasis, right lower-lobe consolidation, and right middle-lobe consolidation. Bacterial co-detection profile Among the 309 infants, Streptococcus pneumoniae (SP) was the most frequently co-detected bacterium, with 152 detections (49.2%), followed by Haemophilus influenzae (HI) in 119 cases (38.5%), Staphylococcus aureus (SA) in 61 cases (19.7%), Moraxella catarrhalis in 32 cases (10.4%), Escherichia coli in 29 cases (9.4%), Acinetobacter baumannii in 11 cases (3.6%), Klebsiella pneumoniae in 10 cases (3.2%), Pseudomonas aeruginosa in 8 cases (2.6%), Klebsiella oxytoca in 3 cases (1.0%), Enterobacter hormaechei in 2 cases (0.6%), and several other bacteria in 1 case each (0.3%). A single bacterial species was co-detected in 209 infants (67.6%) (Table 1), whereas two or more bacterial species were co-detected in 100 infants (32.4%), including 77 double detections (24.9%) and 23 detections of three or more bacterial species (7.5%) (Table 2). These findings describe the bacterial DNA profile of cases retained after clinical adjudication and exclusion of cases considered to represent airway colonization. Age and sex did not differ significantly between groups. Delivery mode, complications, poor appetite, vomiting, nasal congestion, and rhinorrhea were not significantly different (Table 3). The assessment considered respiratory distress, hypoxemia, systemic toxicity or altered mental status, severe complications, and the need for intensive supportive care. Infants who did not meet the severe-disease criteria were classified as non- severe. The study was approved by the Ethics Committee of Henan Children's Hospital (2025-IITGC-011- 001), which waived the requirement for informed consent because of the retrospective observational design. Specimen collection and microbiological testing Deep sputum, blood, and nasopharyngeal swab specimens were collected by trained staff using aseptic procedures within 24 h of admission and were tested in the institutional clinical laboratory. hMPV and bacterial targets were identified from routine nucleic-acid reports, and culture results were recorded when available. Pathogen-load information was extracted when reported. No additional microbiological testing was performed for this study. Clinical adjudication of bacterial infection versus airway colonization Bacterial colonization and possible concomitant bacterial pneumonia were differentiated by integrating clinical deterioration, inflammatory markers, chest imaging, reported pathogen load, culture results when available, and the treating team’s documented response assessment.
